GateChat: A Federated, Confidence-Gated Chatbot  We propose a distributed chatbot where a System 1 model answers a user's question from a set of known options when it is confident, and passes uncertain questions to a larger language model. The System 1 model is trained with federated learning: several workers improve it on their own private data and share only model updates, never the raw data. The system runs across multiple nodes, using Kafka for messaging, Redis for shared state and Kubernetes for deployment and recovery. The distributed concepts we will implement ourselves include round coordination with tolerance for stragglers, exactly-once handling of each query, backpressure under load, and failure detection with failover between replicas. We will show concurrent operation across several machines, recovery from injected failures such as killing a node.

We are interested in infrastructure-style systems work, and any of our three preferences would suit us. For #38, we plan to use a small open model (e.g., GPT-2) with PyTorch, split layers across worker processes over gRPC, and handle per-request KV-cache state, micro-batching, and recovery from worker crashes. For #28, we would implement the consensus-backed partition-ownership service ourselves using Raft in Go, rather than relying on an existing library. For #24, we would likewise implement Raft ourselves to order and replicate signed transactions across nodes. If none of these are available, we would prefer #49, #34, or #2, in that order.
